findings: Count scaling35/history_days is algebraically appropriate for linearly accumulated counts under constant expected daily rate. Column5 schedule-adjusted count also scales linearly because airing rate ratio is already normalized by period length.
Decay factor (1-exp(-ln2*35/half_life))/(1-exp(-ln2*history_days/half_life)) is the correct ratio of integrated exponential decay mass for homogeneous arrivals.
Transformation is mathematically identity on nominal35day fitting histories, so no refit is required to test this heuristic. This does not establish identical train/test distributions.
AP@5 denominator, cold popularity fallback and deterministic tie handling remain unchanged. Transformation uses known history duration, no future viewing labels.
Distinct watched-airing-day scaling assumes stable daily event probability, which may fail for user entry, churn, or seasonality.
Historical unique-viewer popularity and user distinct-item count remain unadjusted; these are history-dependent but not generally linear in time.
For logistic regression, user-total feature changes only a within-user constant and cannot itself change rankings; for boosting it can interact with other features.
Actual normalized fitting history is34days23hours because of civil clock correction; nominal35days is a negligible approximation but identity is nominal, not physical elapsed-time exact.
Post-hoc choice among variants reuses explored overlapping validation windows and must be reported as selection, not independent confirmation.
